# Jubilees Chapter 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob visits Isaac; Isaac blesses Levi and Judah

---

**31:1** And Jacob went and came to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah at Mamre, which is the valley of Hebron, in the second year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

**31:2** And Jacob hid Rachel and Leah and his handmaids and all his sons and his daughter and all his cattle and his cattle-herds and all his possessions. He dwelt in his father's house at Mamre.

**31:3** And on the new moon of the seventh month, Isaac his father held a feast. And he sent and called Jacob his son. And he came and brought a gift to his father.

**31:4** And Jacob feared to go in to his father, for his father was old and his eyes were dim. But his mother Rebekah said to him: "Fear not; go in to him."

**31:5** And Jacob came in to his father Isaac, who stretched out his hands and embraced him and wept upon his neck. And he kissed him on the face and said to him: "My son, I am old, and mine eyes are dim, and I see thee not, but thy fragrance I smell, and thy voice I hear."

**31:6** And Jacob said to his father: "I am Jacob thy son who loveth thee as it is fitting that a son should love his father."

**31:7** And Isaac said to him: "Why hast thou come, my son?" And Jacob said: "I came to see thee and to kiss thy hands and thy face and to bless thee, and to request that thou pray for me."

**31:8** And Isaac held his son Jacob and embraced and kissed him, and wept greatly.

**31:9** And Isaac called his son Levi and said to him: "Come near to me." And Levi came near, and Isaac placed his right hand upon his head and put his left hand upon his shoulder.

**31:10** And he said: "May the God of all, the Lord of all ages, bless thee and thy sons throughout all the generations of the age. And may the LORD thy God make thee and thy seed to be a priestly people unto him, the most holy of all peoples, for all ages."

**31:11** "And may he give thee and thy seed and the seed of thy seed all the greatness of the priesthood that can be given. And thou shalt be holy and great before God. And thy seed shall be exalted and accepted before him."

**31:12** "And thou shalt be a servant of God's sanctuary and blessed and sanctified. Be a prince among the sons of God, and may all peoples be subject to thee, and may thy sons and the sons of thy sons be holy."

**31:13** "And he has chosen thee from among all flesh to serve him, and to minister before him in his sanctuary, and to be his minister and a blessing in the midst of all the earth."

**31:14** And he let Levi depart and called Judah near to him, and put his right hand upon his head and said:

**31:15** "May the LORD God of all bless thee forever, my son. And may he give thee power and greatness for victory over all the nations of the earth, and for all peoples who do not know thee to fear thy name, and all the kings of the earth to be afraid before thee."

**31:16** "And may thy fruit be many and thy seed be made great. And may thy rule be great in the earth. And be exalted, my son, and strengthen the power of thy seed."

**31:17** "And be a king and a prince among all the peoples, and may all nations bow before thee."

**31:18** And he put both hands on his head and kissed him and said: "May the LORD God bless thee, the holy God of Israel who rules over all the earth. May he sanctify thee and choose thee as a holy people."

**31:19** And Jacob was glad, and blessed and praised God, and fell on his face before his father Isaac and bowed down.

**31:20** And the spirit of prophecy descended upon Isaac's mouth, and he said: "Blessed art thou, O LORD God of Israel who hast kept me and all the generations of my fathers, of those who did not transgress thy covenant and thy ordinances. And thou hast blessed Jacob and blessed Levi and Judah."

**31:21** And he arose and wept when he saw Jacob's sons standing there, twelve in number. And he was glad, and he blessed them all.

**31:22** And Jacob went from the presence of Isaac his father that day, glad and rejoicing. He told the good news to Rebekah his mother.

---

*EMET notes: Isaac's blessing of Levi (vv.9-13) and Judah (vv.14-18) in Jubilees expands the Genesis account significantly. The priestly blessing of Levi here anticipates the Levitical legislation of later chapters. The spirit of prophecy descending upon Isaac (v.20) is a distinctive Jubilees motif.*
